DIAGNOSIS READY: Distal Intestinal Obstruction (likely Hirschsprung Disease).

The abdominal X-ray confirms dilated bowel segments with no gas in the rectum, indicating a blockage. Given the infant's age and the absence of a meconium-like stool, this strongly suggests a failure of the bowel to relax, such as in Hirschsprung disease.
